Keep a Warehouse if you want T-SQL-first ELT, stored procedures or multi-table transactions." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="38" width="466" x="84" y="737" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c134" parent="1" style="ellipse;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#C2410C;strokeWidth=1.5;fontSize=10;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#C2410C;" value="6" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="20" width="20" x="568" y="724" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c135" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=10;fontColor=#1F1F1F;fontStyle=1;" value="Fabric governs; Purview extends" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="16" width="466" x="594" y="721" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c136" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=9;fontColor=#5C5C5C;fontStyle=0;" value="Catalog, lineage and sensitivity labels are part of Fabric, and Purview adds classification and DLP across the wider estate. Access is set per path, so plan it for the SQL endpoint as well as the model." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="38" width="466" x="594" y="737" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c137" parent="1" style="ellipse;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#BDBDBD;strokeWidth=1.5;fontSize=10;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#5C5C5C;" value="i" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="20" width="20" x="1078" y="724" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c138" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=10;fontColor=#1F1F1F;fontStyle=1;" value="Analytical storage is OneLake" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="16" width="466" x="1104" y="721" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c139" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=9;fontColor=#5C5C5C;fontStyle=0;" value="OneDrive and SharePoint can be sources or destinations, but they are not the lake. The other rename worth knowing: Power BI <i>datasets</i> are now <i>semantic models</i>." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="38" width="466" x="1104" y="737" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c140" parent="1" style="ellipse;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#C2410C;strokeWidth=1.5;fontSize=10;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#C2410C;" value="7" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="20" width="20" x="1588" y="724" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c141" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=10;fontColor=#1F1F1F;fontStyle=1;" value="Controlled exports, and their limits" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="16" width="466" x="1614" y="721" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c142" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=9;fontColor=#5C5C5C;fontStyle=0;" value="A scheduled export runs under its own identity, not the recipient's, so distribution has to be designed. Fabric lineage stays in the service, and a Power BI export carries its sensitivity label to Excel but not to CSV." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="38" width="466" x="1614" y="737" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c143" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=10;fontColor=#5C5C5C;fontStyle=0;" value="<b>Where the measured figures come from.</b> 27,307,478 rows landed into the bronze lakehouse in 10m31s through one gateway, reconciled 77/77 &#8212; every row count and control total exact. That run used Db2 LUW 11.5.9 on an Azure VM as a stand-in, so connectivity and throughput against Equation on Db2 for i still have to be proven separately." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="16" width="2040" x="40" y="786" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c144" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=10;fontColor=#5C5C5C;fontStyle=0;" value="<b>Two limits worth stating up front.</b> The Db2 connector is source-only, so Fabric never writes back to Equation. And a watermark &#8212; had it worked &#8212; would still never capture deletes, because a row that is gone cannot carry a changed timestamp. Periodic full reconciliation, or journals, are the answers to that." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="16" width="2040" x="40" y="806" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: Copy job offers a timestamp-watermark option and even finds the row-change column — but the incremental run failed in testing, reproduced on one 109-row table. There is no Mirroring for Db2 either. A full load is the validated path, and at 10m31s it still beats the manual one.

div.div: Transformation happens after the landing

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 702px; margin-left: 1078px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;

div.div: In Fabric, data lands raw in bronze first; notebooks or Dataflow Gen2 then read bronze and write silver and gold. That keeps a replayable landing and makes a reload deterministic.

div.div: The medallion, and where bad rows go

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 702px; margin-left: 1588px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 9px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5C5C5C, #9e9e9e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Bronze, silver and gold give each step one job. Rows that fail a rule are set aside with the rule and batch that caught them, rather than dropped or silently included.

ellipse.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(194, 65, 12), rgb(251, 140, 94));

display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 727px; margin-left: 58px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #1F1F1F;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1F1F1F, #d2d2d2); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Lakehouse here; Warehouse still an option

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 754px; margin-left: 58px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 9px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5C5C5C, #9e9e9e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Fabric asks you to pick by development style, and this build is Delta and Spark first. Every lakehouse also exposes a read-only T-SQL endpoint. Keep a Warehouse if you want T-SQL-first ELT, stored procedures or multi-table transactions.

ellipse.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(194, 65, 12), rgb(251, 140, 94));

div.div: Fabric governs; Purview extends

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 754px; margin-left: 568px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 9px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5C5C5C, #9e9e9e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Catalog, lineage and sensitivity labels are part of Fabric, and Purview adds classification and DLP across the wider estate. Access is set per path, so plan it for the SQL endpoint as well as the model.

div.div: Analytical storage is OneLake

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 754px; margin-left: 1078px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 9px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5C5C5C, #9e9e9e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: OneDrive and SharePoint can be sources or destinations, but they are not the lake. The other rename worth knowing: Power BI datasets are now semantic models.

ellipse.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(194, 65, 12), rgb(251, 140, 94));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 18px; height: 1px; padding-top: 732px; margin-left: 1561px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #C2410C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#C2410C, #fb8c5e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 727px; margin-left: 1588px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #1F1F1F;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1F1F1F, #d2d2d2); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Controlled exports, and their limits

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 464px; height: 1px; padding-top: 754px; margin-left: 1588px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 9px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5C5C5C, #9e9e9e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: A scheduled export runs under its own identity, not the recipient's, so distribution has to be designed. Fabric lineage stays in the service, and a Power BI export carries its sensitivity label to Excel but not to CSV.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 2038px; height: 1px; padding-top: 792px; margin-left: 14px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5C5C5C, #9e9e9e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Where the measured figures come from. 27,307,478 rows landed into the bronze lakehouse in 10m31s through one gateway, reconciled 77/77 — every row count and control total exact. That run used Db2 LUW 11.5.9 on an Azure VM as a stand-in, so connectivity and throughput against Equation on Db2 for i still have to be proven separately.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 2038px; height: 1px; padding-top: 812px; margin-left: 14px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #5C5C5C;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5C5C5C, #9e9e9e); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Two limits worth stating up front. The Db2 connector is source-only, so Fabric never writes back to Equation. And a watermark — had it worked — would still never capture deletes, because a row that is gone cannot carry a changed timestamp. Periodic full reconciliation, or journals, are the answers to that.
